subject: general
question: What is the mineral name of rock salt?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Halite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Halite **commonly known as **rock salt**, is a type of salt, the **mineral (**natural) form of **sodium chloride **(NaCl).
 
• **Halite **forms **isometric crystals**.
 
• **Halite **is mainly a **sedimentary mineral **that usually forms in **arid climates where ocean water evaporates**.
 
• **Salt **is widely used in **cooking **as a **taste enhancer and **in the curing of a **number of foods, including bacon and fish**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Limonite **is a general term for **a mixture of fine-grained iron oxides**, generally dominated by **goethite**, but also **possibly containing hematite, lepidocrocite, and other minerals**.
 
• **Hematite**, also spelt **haematite**, **heavy **and **relatively hard oxide mineral, ferric oxide **(**Fe2O3**), that **constitutes the most important iron ore **because of its **high iron content **(70 per cent) and **its abundance.**
 
• **Siderite**, also called **chalybite**, is an **iron carbonate (FeCO3), **a widespread mineral that is **iron ore**. The **mineral commonly occurs **in thin **beds with shales**, **clay**, or **coal seams **(sedimentary deposits) and in **hydrothermal metallic veins **(gangue, or waste rock).
